title: First justification free; second (growth) from condign merit of works
source_text: LI. Attamen Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae distinctionem hic adhibent inter justificationem primam, qua homo ex peccatore & impio fit justus & sanctus, per peccati remissionem, & per adoptionem gratiae sanctificantis atque regenerantis, & inter justificationem secundam, qua homo jam justificatus in justitia & sanctitate crescit, & ex justo justior, ex sancto sanctior evadit. Et prima quidem illa est quam gratuitam esse volunt; sed quod attinet ad secundam justificationem, docent illam esse ex meritis, & hominem justum sic per bona opera in justitia & sanctitate crescere, ut etiam ex condigno, mereatur augmentum gratiae sanctificantis, atque justificantis.
pass_a_gloss: Nevertheless the Doctors of the Roman Church here apply a distinction between first justification, by which a man from a sinner and ungodly becomes just and holy, through remission of sin and through adoption of sanctifying and regenerating grace, and second justification, by which a man already justified grows in righteousness and holiness, and from just becomes more just, from holy more holy. And the former indeed is what they will to be gratuitous; but as for second justification, they teach that it is from merits, and that the just man so grows through good works in righteousness and holiness that even from condignity he merits an increase of sanctifying and justifying grace.
pass_b_english: Rome: first justification (sinner→just) is free gift.
Second justification (growth) they ground in condign merit of good works.

choices.english: from condignity, merits an increase of grace
choices.why: Key Roman claim on growth after first grace.
rejected: all growth remains non-meritorious gift only
